confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership. Tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.327, q=0.003), CT manufacturer (0.344, q=0.00675), CT scanner model (0.260, q=0.0072), CT phase (0.182, q=0.0465), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.310, q=1.37e-05), and CT z-spacing (0.310, q=1.37e-05) all remain associated after BH correction within their respective families. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and study year (q=0.364) are not significant after correction, and CT pixel spacing shows no detectable association (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.966). These are partition-wide associations: they indicate that measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for the partition as a whole and may motivate candidate-specific follow-up. They do not establish that any particular candidate has a candidate-specific confounder association, and association is not causation. Nonsignificance for kernel, study year, and pixel spacing does not establish absence of confounding.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: These partition-scope associations are consistent with the confounder_representation_effect report, which shows significant PERMANOVA for several of the same factors (tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT slice thickness, CT z-spacing, study year) and significant PERMDISP for CT manufacturer and CT phase. Together they indicate a partition-wide technical concern rather than a candidate-specific one.
limitations: Partition-scope association describes a partition-wide technical concern and must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association.
Association is not causation; a significant test is not proof of technical artifact.

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership. Tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.327, q=0.003), CT manufacturer (0.344, q=0.00675), CT scanner model (0.260, q=0.0072), CT phase (0.182, q=0.0465), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.310, q=1.37e-05), and CT z-spacing (0.310, q=1.37e-05) all remain associated after BH correction within their respective families. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and study year (q=0.364) are not significant after correction, and CT pixel spacing shows no detectable association (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.966). These are partition-wide associations: they indicate that measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for the partition as a whole and may motivate candidate-specific follow-up. They do not establish that any particular candidate has a candidate-specific confounder association, and association is not causation. Nonsignificance for kernel, study year, and pixel spacing does not establish absence of confounding.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: These partition-scope associations are consistent with the confounder_representation_effect report, which shows significant PERMANOVA for several of the same factors (tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT slice thickness, CT z-spacing, study year) and significant PERMDISP for CT manufacturer and CT phase. Together they indicate a partition-wide technical concern rather than a candidate-specific one.
limitations: Partition-scope association describes a partition-wide technical concern and must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association.
Association is not causation; a significant test is not proof of technical artifact.
Nonsignificance (kernel, study year, pixel spacing) does not establish absence of confounding.

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership. Tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.327, q=0.003), CT manufacturer (0.344, q=0.00675), CT scanner model (0.260, q=0.0072), CT phase (0.182, q=0.0465), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.310, q=1.37e-05), and CT z-spacing (0.310, q=1.37e-05) all remain associated after BH correction within their respective families. Nonsignificance for kernel, study year, and pixel spacing does not establish absence of confounding.

reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership. confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership. Tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.327, q=0.003), CT manufacturer (0.344, q=0.00675), CT scanner model (0.260, q=0.0072), CT phase (0.182, q=0.0465), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.310, q=1.37e-05), and CT z-spacing (0.310, q=1.37e-05) all remain associated after BH correction within their respective families. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and study year (q=0.364) are not significant after correction, and CT pixel spacing shows no detectable association (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.966). These are partition-wide associations: they indicate that measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for the partition as a whole and may motivate candidate-specific follow-up. They do not establish that any particular candidate has a candidate-specific confounder association, and association is not causation. Nonsignificance for kernel, study year, and pixel spacing does not establish absence of confounding.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: These partition-scope associations are consistent with the confounder_representation_effect report, which shows significant PERMANOVA for several of the same factors (tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT slice thickness, CT z-spacing, study year) and significant PERMDISP for CT manufacturer and CT phase. Together they indicate a partition-wide technical concern rather than a candidate-specific one.

CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and study year (q=0.364) are not significant after correction, and CT pixel spacing shows no detectable association (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.966). These are partition-wide associations: they indicate that measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for the partition as a whole and may motivate candidate-specific follow-up. They do not establish that any particular candidate has a candidate-specific confounder association, and association is not causation. Nonsignificance for kernel, study year, and pixel spacing does not establish absence of confounding.
reports.cross_evidence_context: These partition-scope associations are consistent with the confounder_representation_effect report, which shows significant PERMANOVA for several of the same factors (tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT slice thickness, CT z-spacing, study year) and significant PERMDISP for CT manufacturer and CT phase. Together they indicate a partition-wide technical concern rather than a candidate-specific one.
limitations: Partition-scope association describes a partition-wide technical concern and must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association.
Association is not causation; a significant test is not proof of technical artifact.
Nonsignificance (kernel, study year, pixel spacing) does not establish absence of confounding.
Categorical and continuous factor p-values belong to separate BH families and are not directly comparable.
Factor imbalance and coverage vary across levels (e.g., CT manufacturer GE 70 vs Philips 3), which limits inference for sparse levels.

reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors are associated with the geometry. Tissue source site shows the largest PERMANOVA association (r-squared 0.204, q=0.0025) with no significant dispersion difference (PERMDISP p=0.471), consistent with a location/centroid association. CT phase (r-squared 0.154, q=0.0025) and CT manufacturer (r-squared 0.059, q=0.00667) show significant PERMANOVA together with significant PERMDISP (q=0.0285 and q=0.009), so their PERMANOVA may reflect both location and dispersion differences. Continuous CT factors show significant distance-regression associations: slice thickness (r-squared 0.136, q=0.002), z-spacing (r-squared 0.142, q=0.002), study year (r-squared 0.029, q=0.004), and pixel spacing (r-squared 0.019, q=0.035). CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and CT scanner model (q=0.054) are not significant after correction, and their PERMDISP is not estimable because some levels have fewer than two observations. These are partition-wide associations indicating that measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for the partition geometry; they do not establish technical artifact or causation, and nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding.
reports.cross_evidence_context: These geometry associations align with the confounder_association report: the same factors (tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT slice thickness, CT z-spacing) are significant in both the categorical/numeric association tests and the geometry-based tests, reinforcing a partition-wide technical concern. PERMANOVA, PERMDISP, and continuous distance-regression p-values belong to separate BH families and are not directly comparable.
limitations: Partition-scope association describes a partition-wide technical concern and must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K7_C0004, the four native patient geometries provide weak and partly conflicting evidence about current membership representation. RNA shows weak positive separation (silhouette 0.044, negative fraction 0.28). CT (-0.017, negative fraction 0.50) and WSI (-0.004, negative fraction 0.39) are essentially null, with within-label distances marginally exceeding or matching between-label distances. WXS shows clear negative separation (-0.317, negative fraction 0.78), with mean within-label distance exceeding mean between-label distance. Synthesized jointly rather than by vote counting, the overall native-view pattern is weak-to-conflicting: no view shows more than marginal positive separation, and genomic geometry is reversed. Nearest competing sets differ by modality (CT K7_C0005; RNA K7_C0007; WSI and WXS K7_C0001). This bears directly on membership representation but does not by itself determine accept or drop.
reports.cross_evidence_context: Prior pair-scope reports involving K7_C0004 are consistent with this weak-to-conflicting picture: K7_C0001-K7_C0004 and K7_C0004-K7_C0006 are weak-to-conflicting, K7_C0002-K7_C0004 and K7_C0004-K7_C0007 are weak positive. Prior biological report describes K7_C0004 as an immune-low, TGF-beta-high transcriptomic identity. Prior confounder report flags significant candidate-specific associations for CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT slice thickness, and CT z-spacing as plausible alternative explanations for this set's membership.
limitations: Set-scope alignment uses full current partition labels; it does not address pair boundaries or full-partition membership decisions.

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership. Tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.327, q=0.003), CT manufacturer (0.344, q=0.00675), CT scanner model (0.260, q=0.0072), CT phase (0.182, q=0.0465), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.310, q=1.37e-05), and CT z-spacing (0.310, q=1.37e-05) all remain associated after BH correction within their respective families. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and study year (q=0.364) are not significant after correction, and CT pixel spacing shows no detectable association (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.966). These are partition-wide associations: they indicate that measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for the partition as a whole and may motivate candidate-specific follow-up. They do not establish that any particular candidate has a candidate-specific confounder association, and association is not causation. Nonsignificance for kernel, study year, and pixel spacing does not establish absence of confounding.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: These partition-scope associations are consistent with the confounder_representation_effect report, which shows significant PERMANOVA for several of the same factors (tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT slice thickness, CT z-spacing, study year) and significant PERMDISP for CT manufacturer and CT phase. Together they indicate a partition-wide technical concern rather than a candidate-specific one.
limitations: Partition-scope association describes a partition-wide technical concern and must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association.
Association is not causation; a significant test is not proof of technical artifact.

reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership. confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership. Tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.327, q=0.003), CT manufacturer (0.344, q=0.00675), CT scanner model (0.260, q=0.0072), CT phase (0.182, q=0.0465), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.310, q=1.37e-05), and CT z-spacing (0.310, q=1.37e-05) all remain associated after BH correction within their respective families. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and study year (q=0.364) are not significant after correction, and CT pixel spacing shows no detectable association (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.966). These are partition-wide associations: they indicate that measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for the partition as a whole and may motivate candidate-specific follow-up. They do not establish that any particular candidate has a candidate-specific confounder association, and association is not causation. Nonsignificance for kernel, study year, and pixel spacing does not establish absence of confounding.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: These partition-scope associations are consistent with the confounder_representation_effect report, which shows significant PERMANOVA for several of the same factors (tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT slice thickness, CT z-spacing, study year) and significant PERMDISP for CT manufacturer and CT phase. Together they indicate a partition-wide technical concern rather than a candidate-specific one.
limitations: Partition-scope association describes a partition-wide technical concern and must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association.
Association is not causation; a significant test is not proof of technical artifact.

reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership. Tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.327, q=0.003), CT manufacturer (0.344, q=0.00675), CT scanner model (0.260, q=0.0072), CT phase (0.182, q=0.0465), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.310, q=1.37e-05), and CT z-spacing (0.310, q=1.37e-05) all remain associated after BH correction within their respective families. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and study year (q=0.364) are not significant after correction, and CT pixel spacing shows no detectable association (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.966). These are partition-wide associations: they indicate that measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for the partition as a whole and may motivate candidate-specific follow-up. They do not establish that any particular candidate has a candidate-specific confounder association, and association is not causation. Nonsignificance for kernel, study year, and pixel spacing does not establish absence of confounding.
reports.cross_evidence_context: These partition-scope associations are consistent with the confounder_representation_effect report, which shows significant PERMANOVA for several of the same factors (tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT slice thickness, CT z-spacing, study year) and significant PERMDISP for CT manufacturer and CT phase. Together they indicate a partition-wide technical concern rather than a candidate-specific one.
limitations: Partition-scope association describes a partition-wide technical concern and must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association.
Association is not causation; a significant test is not proof of technical artifact.
Nonsignificance (kernel, study year, pixel spacing) does not establish absence of confounding.

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership. Tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.327, q=0.003), CT manufacturer (0.344, q=0.00675), CT scanner model (0.260, q=0.0072), CT phase (0.182, q=0.0465), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.310, q=1.37e-05), and CT z-spacing (0.310, q=1.37e-05) all remain associated after BH correction within their respective families. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and study year (q=0.364) are not significant after correction, and CT pixel spacing shows no detectable association (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.966). These are partition-wide associations: they indicate that measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for the partition as a whole and may motivate candidate-specific follow-up. They do not establish that any particular candidate has a candidate-specific confounder association, and association is not causation. Nonsignificance for kernel, study year, and pixel spacing does not establish absence of confounding.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: These partition-scope associations are consistent with the confounder_representation_effect report, which shows significant PERMANOVA for several of the same factors (tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT slice thickness, CT z-spacing, study year) and significant PERMDISP for CT manufacturer and CT phase. Together they indicate a partition-wide technical concern rather than a candidate-specific one.
limitations: Partition-scope association describes a partition-wide technical concern and must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association.
Association is not causation; a significant test is not proof of technical artifact.

reports.dimension_interpretation: At partition scope, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant association with candidate membership. Tissue source site (Cramer's V 0.327, q=0.003), CT manufacturer (0.344, q=0.00675), CT scanner model (0.260, q=0.0072), CT phase (0.182, q=0.0465), CT slice thickness (epsilon-squared 0.310, q=1.37e-05), and CT z-spacing (0.310, q=1.37e-05) all remain associated after BH correction within their respective families. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and study year (q=0.364) are not significant after correction, and CT pixel spacing shows no detectable association (epsilon-squared 0.0, q=0.966). These are partition-wide associations: they indicate that measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for the partition as a whole and may motivate candidate-specific follow-up. They do not establish that any particular candidate has a candidate-specific confounder association, and association is not causation. Nonsignificance for kernel, study year, and pixel spacing does not establish absence of confounding.
reports.cross_evidence_context: These partition-scope associations are consistent with the confounder_representation_effect report, which shows significant PERMANOVA for several of the same factors (tissue source site, CT phase, CT manufacturer, CT slice thickness, CT z-spacing, study year) and significant PERMDISP for CT manufacturer and CT phase. Together they indicate a partition-wide technical concern rather than a candidate-specific one.
limitations: Partition-scope association describes a partition-wide technical concern and must not be presented as a candidate-specific confounder association.
Association is not causation; a significant test is not proof of technical artifact.
Nonsignificance (kernel, study year, pixel spacing) does not establish absence of confounding.

Tissue source site shows the largest PERMANOVA association (r-squared 0.204, q=0.0025) with no significant dispersion difference (PERMDISP p=0.471), consistent with a location/centroid association. CT phase (r-squared 0.154, q=0.0025) and CT manufacturer (r-squared 0.059, q=0.00667) show significant PERMANOVA together with significant PERMDISP (q=0.0285 and q=0.009), so their PERMANOVA may reflect both location and dispersion differences. CT reconstruction kernel (q=0.054) and CT scanner model (q=0.054) are not significant after correction, and their PERMDISP is not estimable because some levels have fewer than two observations. These are partition-wide associations indicating that measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternative explanations for the partition geometry; they do not establish technical artifact or causation, and nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding.
